title: Trip Protection: Buying a Plan and How the Premium Is Set
content:
A Trip Protection plan is bought for one stay, and the premium is set from the insured trip cost at the rate and minimum of the plan bought. Premiums charged are booked to the policy's premiums as money in, and premium refunds as money out.

## Rules of sale

1. **When a plan may be bought.** A plan may be bought at booking or up to the plan's latest purchase point, stated in calendar days before check-in.
2. **CFAR purchase window.** A Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR) plan can be bought only within the plan's CFAR purchase window, in calendar days after the stay was booked. The days are counted from the date part of the stay's booking moment to the date part of the policy's purchase moment, and a purchase on the last day stands. The booking moment is the one on the system record of the stay the policy insures; the guest's own account of when they booked does not replace it.
3. **Pre-existing condition waiver.** The waiver applies only where the plan includes the pre-existing condition waiver and the plan was bought within the plan's waiver purchase period after booking.

## Premium

The premium is the plan's premium rate (a percentage) of the insured trip cost; where that amount is lower than the plan's minimum premium, it is raised to the minimum; the result is rounded under the plan's premium rounding. Each plan uses its own premium rate and its own minimum premium.

**Change in the stay's price.** When an accepted alteration changes the stay's total price, the insured trip cost and the premium are recomputed under the same rule. An increase in premium is charged to the guest as a further premium; a decrease is refunded to the guest as premium.

## Worked examples (hypothetical plan figures, for illustration only)

Take an illustrative premium rate of 5.00 percent and an illustrative minimum of 20.00 USD.

| Insured trip cost | Rate amount | Compared with the minimum | Premium after rounding to the nearest cent, half up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1234.56 USD | 61.728 USD | above 20.00 | 61.73 USD |
| 300.00 USD | 15.00 USD | below 20.00, raised | 20.00 USD |
| 400.00 USD | 20.00 USD | equal to 20.00 | 20.00 USD |

**Alteration, price up.** Insured trip cost 1000.00 USD gives a premium of 50.00 USD. An accepted alteration raises the stay's total price to 1200.00 USD; the new premium is 60.00 USD and a further premium of 10.00 USD is charged.

**Alteration, price down to the minimum.** Insured trip cost 500.00 USD gives a premium of 25.00 USD. An accepted alteration lowers the total price to 300.00 USD; the rate amount of 15.00 USD is raised to the 20.00 USD minimum, the new premium is 20.00 USD, and 5.00 USD is refunded as premium.

## CFAR purchase window on the boundary

For a CFAR plan with a purchase window of N calendar days and a stay booked on a given date (whatever the time of day):

| Date part of the purchase moment | Result |
|---|---|
| The booking date itself | Within the window |
| The Nth calendar day after the booking date | Within the window; a purchase on the last day stands |
| The calendar day after that | Outside the window; the CFAR plan cannot be bought |

The time of day does not enter the count: a stay booked at 23:50 and a plan bought at 00:10 the following morning are one calendar day apart.
